description: Tests how words someone is about to send will be received — whether an email will land well, how it comes across, whether it could be misunderstood, whether it sounds too harsh, what a manager might misunderstand. Three cold readers (a distracted stranger, a skeptic, and the target reader), each reading cold and never seeing the others, test how the message is actually received against the sender's stated goal. When the words leave gaps only the author can fill (the readers cannot find the point, the proof, or the specifics), the first result has status 'questions_first' and carries up to three short questions built from the readers' own complaints about this text, plus what the readers heard and where they split; a second call with the same text and motivation plus the author's answers returns the sharper, enriched verdict, and a second call with skip_questions true returns the verdict on the words as they stand. A verdict returns four plain grades out of 5, graded directly by the same readers in the same cold read (Easy to read, Holds your attention, The point lands, You'd pass it on; medians across the three readers); for conversation moments (a what's new update, a hard text) a walk_away pair: the thought the author wants the reader to leave with, from the goal, against the thought the readers may actually leave with, from what they heard; the core the readers heard (or the plain split when they heard different points); the readers' own notes including where they split; six SUCCESs medians with the spread between readers and a one-line reason each (the diagnostic layer underneath the plain grades); starter forms only (a proverb line, a curiosity-gap opener, a 3-4 sentence mini-story, concrete swaps for abstract phrases); the one prioritized fix for the element that most blocks the stated goal; and after_text: the draft copied exactly with only that one fix applied by a dedicated guarded step, when the bound passes (null when the bound discards it, with after_reason saying why; changed_lines counts the lines that differ). The tool tests reception only: it never rewrites the draft in full, and it does not shorten, fix grammar, translate, or do generic 'make this clearer' rewriting — a finished transformed version is the output of make_it_stick, which runs the same readers. A check takes roughly ten to twenty seconds; the readers read in sequence and are not instant. Words sent to this tool are not recorded or kept; the server keeps only a daily count of how many checks ran (integers, no text). The three readers run on Cloudflare Workers AI (Meta Llama 3.3 70B); under Cloudflare's published Workers AI terms, text is not retained once it is no longer needed to answer, and it is never used to train AI models. The tool sends nothing; what gets sent stays the author's decision.

answers.description: Answers to a previous questions_first result, in the author's own words. Pass the same text and motivation, plus these, to get the enriched verdict.

answer.description: The author's answer, in a few words.

question.description: The question as the tool asked it.

moment.description: Optional moment name, e.g. 'what's new', 'recommend something', 'a story I tell', 'say thanks', 'ask or invite', 'a hard text'. Helps the target reader sit in the right seat.

motivation.description: One line: what should these words do? Who should do, feel, or remember what? Example: 'Get a friend to actually try the book I loved.'

skip_questions.description: Set true when the author declined the follow-up questions: returns the verdict on the words as they stand.

text.description: The exact words to check: a message, note, toast, post, or pitch. A few sentences up to about 900 words.
